clue.text: Small volume about oil treatment for abdominal trouble

indicators.note: the small-volume letters go round the reworked oil, as about means surrounding

parts.note: cc, cubic centimetres, is a small measure of volume

indicators.note: the word oil is given a treatment, so its letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A remedy of oil for a small measure of stomach pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' rearranges OIL to OLI, and 'about' puts CC round it: C-OLI-C.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is acute spasmodic pain in the belly, a classic stomach complaint.

clue.text: N or M in C of E being the A to its opening Q

definitions.text: N or M in C of E being the A to its opening Q

parts.words: N or M in C of E being the A to its opening Q
parts.note: in the Church of England prayer book's question-and-answer teaching, the first question asks your name and the reply is printed as N or M

explanation.surface: A coded string of letters about the Church of England.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Book of Common Prayer the first Question is 'What is your Name?', Answer 'N. or M.', a placeholder for the name. C of E is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the prayer-book instruction in doctrine set out as questions and answers.

clue.text: Arsène's bloomer

parts.note: the surname of Leblanc's fictional gentleman thief, Arsène, is also the name of a flowering plant

explanation.surface: A mistake made by someone called Arsène.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flower. Arsène Lupin is the French gentleman burglar of Maurice Leblanc's stories.
explanation.definitionFit: The thief's surname doubles as a tall spiked garden flower of the pea family.

clue.text: Spenser's "well of English undefiled"

parts.note: in The Faerie Queene Spenser praised the author of The Canterbury Tales with this phrase

explanation.surface: A quotation from the Elizabethan poet about pure English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' looks like a spring but is Spenser's tribute to his great predecessor.
explanation.definitionFit: Spenser named the medieval poet of The Canterbury Tales the pure source of English verse.

clue.text: Flier Tim has a prang, unhappily

indicators.note: an unhappy outcome after a crash suggests the letters of Tim and a prang are mangled

explanation.surface: A pilot called Tim has crashed his plane, to his dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhappily' rearranges TIM and APRANG into the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The ptarmigan is a grouse of mountain and tundra, a bird and so a flier.

clue.text: Elementary text-book used by painters

definitions.meaning: a first coat put on before the paint

explanation.surface: A beginner's book that decorators use.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a beginner's schoolbook and an undercoat that decorators apply first.

clue.text: Literally the fourth thing an apprentice may be

parts.note: the word the, taken literally, is a definite article
D is the fourth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A riddle about what a trainee might be bound by, in fourth place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' is literally an article; D is the alphabet's fourth.
explanation.definitionFit: An apprentice or trainee solicitor may be bound by articles, a training contract.

clue.text: In Miami a small marsh exudes such vapours

definitions.note: an adjective: the kind of vapours a marsh gives off

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words Miami a small

explanation.surface: A Florida swamp gives off foul fumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals the run hidden in MiaMI A SMALl; a marsh exuding vapours paints the sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Miasma is noxious marsh air once thought to cause disease, so such vapours are miasmal.

clue.text: Cold buffet item at inn perhaps in stormy weather

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed in the word for stormy weather

parts.note: a gale is stormy weather

indicators.note: perhaps hints that at inn is only one possible order of these letters

explanation.surface: Cold meat served at a pub while a storm rages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges AT INN to ANTIN, and 'in' puts it inside GALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Galantine is boned meat pressed in jelly and served cold, a buffet dish.

clue.text: Denial about dry spruce

indicators.note: the denial goes round the dry letters, as about means surrounding

parts.note: nay is a denial, a no
TT, teetotal, means dry

explanation.surface: Refusing a drink while looking smart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts TT inside NAY. 'Spruce' looks like a tree but means smart.
explanation.definitionFit: Spruce as an adjective means neat and smart in dress.

clue.text: Highest one is found in art of this bushman

parts.note: top means highest
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: the word is is found placed inside the word art

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The top artist reckons the finest work lies in his own craft of the bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts IS inside ART, giving ARIST after TOP and I. 'Bushman' is playful: one who shapes bushes, not a dweller in the outback.
explanation.definitionFit: A topiarist clips shrubs into ornamental shapes, so he is jokingly a man of bushes.

clue.text: Distribute a large quantity, say,

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is to be heard as spoken words rather than read

parts.note: a lot means a large quantity

explanation.surface: A request to hand out a great deal, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'a lot' is indistinguishable from the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to share out or assign portions, which is to distribute.

clue.text: A cowardly payment Hamlet appeared to imply

definitions.text: A cowardly payment Hamlet appeared to imply

parts.words: A cowardly payment Hamlet appeared to imply
parts.note: Hamlet says that the inner moral sense makes cowards of us all, so a payment made from guilt is the cowardly one he implies

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's prince seemed to hint at a craven sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet's soliloquy runs 'Thus conscience does make cowards of us all'; money paid to ease a guilty mind is thus 'cowardly' by his logic.
explanation.definitionFit: Such money is paid anonymously to relieve guilt, for example over unpaid tax.

clue.text: Communicate with diabolical skill?

parts.note: an imp is a little devil, so something diabolical suggests an imp
art means skill

explanation.surface: Asking whether talking well is a devilish talent.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as IMP ART, a devil's skill.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart news or knowledge is to pass it on, that is to communicate it.

clue.text: Irritability of uncle with a pet running amok

indicators.note: letters running wild end up in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: An uncle cross because his pet is running wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running amok' scrambles UNCLE and APET.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulance is peevish bad temper, childish irritability.

clue.text: Spring in close proximity almost

parts.note: a well is a spring of water
nigh means near, in close proximity

explanation.surface: A spring that is very close by, nearly.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-nigh is an old-fashioned phrase meaning very nearly.

clue.text: Old farm-hand hurried to church, causing obstruction

parts.note: a hind is an archaic word for a farm worker
ran means hurried
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An old labourer rushed to church and got in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: CE, the Church of England, is crossword shorthand for church.
explanation.definitionFit: A hindrance is something that impedes or blocks progress.

clue.text: It's tossed into the waste pipe — distressing thing to do

indicators.note: into places the shuffled letters inside the pipe word

parts.note: a drain is a waste pipe

indicators.note: letters that are tossed land in a different order

parts.note: it's read as it is, three letters

explanation.surface: Something thrown down the plughole, an upsetting thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossed' turns ITS to IST and 'into' puts it inside DRAIN. In law, distress is seizure of goods for debt.
explanation.definitionFit: To distrain is to seize goods to force payment, the legal act called distress.

clue.text: Like the clink of money that satisfied everyone in charge

parts.note: met all means satisfied everyone, as in meeting all demands

explanation.surface: The sound of cash that kept the person in command happy with all.
explanation.walkthrough: MET ALL + IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Coins are made of metal, so their clink has a metal ring.

clue.text: See, Your Majesty, it is appearing

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
O King is how one addresses a monarch

explanation.surface: Look, sire, here it comes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'O King' is the vocative form of address.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking as in 'looking tired' means seeming or appearing.

clue.text: Clementine's home as lookout used by the Navy

parts.note: cave, Latin for beware, is old schoolboy slang for keep a lookout
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Where Clementine lived served as a naval watch post.
explanation.walkthrough: In the song 'Oh My Darling, Clementine', she lives 'in a cavern, in a canyon'. 'Cave!' was what British schoolboys called to warn of a teacher coming.
explanation.definitionFit: The folk song places the miner's daughter living in a large cave.

clue.text: Former means of distilling drink — 1,001 BC roughly

parts.note: ale is a drink

indicators.note: roughly signals the letters are arranged only approximately, so jumbled

parts.note: MI is the Roman numeral for 1,001

explanation.surface: An ancient still for making alcohol dating from about 1001 BC.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' rearranges MI and BC to MBIC, after ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: An alembic is an old glass still used by alchemists to purify liquids.

clue.text: Thomas of Wessex about fifty? Only just

indicators.note: the novelist's name goes round the fifty letter

parts.note: Thomas Hardy set his novels in Wessex
L is the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: Was the Wessex novelist roughly fifty? Barely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'approximately' but puts HARDY round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardly means barely or scarcely.

clue.text: Don on safari seems in the pink politically

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for a noun: a sympathiser who is pinkish, mildly red, in politics

parts.note: a university don is a fellow of a college
someone on safari is a traveller

explanation.surface: An academic away on safari looks perfectly healthy and leftish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the pink' looks like 'healthy'; here pink is a pale shade of communist red.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a non-member who sympathises with Communist aims, a pinko.

clue.text: Such teeth may be painlessly extracted

definitions.text: Such teeth may be painlessly extracted

parts.words: Such teeth may be painlessly extracted
parts.note: dentures can simply be taken out with no pain at all

explanation.surface: A dentist's reassurance about extractions.
explanation.walkthrough: The extraction sounds like dentistry; these teeth just come out of the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentures are artificial teeth that slip out without any dentist.

clue.text: Slow movement of ancient vessel after opening of leak

indicators.note: after puts the ship behind the first letter
the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts

explanation.surface: An old ship moves slowly after springing a leak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' looks like motion but is a section of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a very slow musical tempo, and a piece or movement in it.

clue.text: After a breather one put on Indian garb

parts.note: a lung is an organ for breathing, a breather
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: After resting, someone dressed in Indian clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After a breather' looks like 'after a rest'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lungi is a cloth wrapped round the waist, worn in India and nearby.

clue.text: Throwing around bread, Alan gets a shiner in The Bull

indicators.note: throwing things around scatters them, so the letters of bread and Alan are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Alan, chucking bread about in a pub called The Bull, ends up with a black eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A shiner' and 'The Bull' read as a black eye in a pub; they mean a star in Taurus, the Bull constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldebaran is the brightest star of the constellation Taurus.

clue.text: In eastern quarter, information of sudden danger

indicators.note: the word in places information within quarter

parts.note: quarter is mercy, as in giving no quarter
gen is slang for information

explanation.surface: News of a sudden threat in the east of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts GEN inside MERCY. 'Quarter' looks like a district but means clemency.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency is a sudden perilous situation needing immediate action.

clue.text: Many adore something spicy

parts.note: C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, stands for many
to adore is to love

explanation.surface: Lots of people adore hot food.
explanation.definitionFit: A clove is a dried flower bud used as a pungent kitchen spice.
